transcript.text: Our Dyson (one of the V ones, purple bits) keeps cutting out after about 5-10 seconds. Not every time - some days it does a whole room fine. It's maybe 5 years old. Already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages. Battery or something else?

Please check that the charger is plugged into a working socket and pushed fully into the vacuum or dock. Wipe the charging contacts clean and dry to ensure they are free from debris. The charging light should then come on. Was the charger, socket or contacts the problem (and is it sorted), does the charging light never come on, or is the charger fine with the light on?
Charger's fine, the light comes on and the plug goes in properly. It charges and shows full blue lights, so I don't think that's the problem.

Thanks for letting us know about the charger light. Please note that running a cordless vacuum in Boost or Max mode will drain the battery very quickly, which is completely normal behaviour. Was it on boost / max mode (and have you switched to normal), or was it already on the normal mode?
It does it on Max mostly, nearly always within a few seconds. On normal mode it's less often, but it still happens sometimes. Is that a sign the battery's on its way out?

[Heading: Worn battery]
From what you've described, a worn battery is the most likely cause, but I can't confirm it from what we know. I'm not recommending a part from this.
Ok. So is it worth spending £60+ on a new battery, or is there something else I should rule out first? The battery isn't swollen or hot, if that matters.

[Heading: Worn battery]
Thanks for the update on your Dyson vacuum. No problem at all — nothing changes from what I said above. If you can't check it, that's fine; an appliance engineer can look at it safely.
